exposure: previous use of the oral contraceptive pill (OCP)
cohort: The study included 760 low-risk pregnant women, recruited into five gestational groups, with a postnatal group also examined.
finding: The study found significant differences in D-dimer levels based on previous OCP use, parity, onset of labor, and mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Elective Caesarean section was associated with significantly lower D-dimer levels compared to spontaneous onset of labor, induction of labor, normal vaginal delivery, instrumental vaginal delivery, and emergency Caesarean section.
cross-section timing: Antenatal groups (specifically 38-40+6 weeks gestation) and a day 2 postnatal group.
gest_age: Women were recruited into five gestational groups, with specific findings noted for the 38-40+6 weeks gestation group.
